steps.message: Drop the requireLogin check on the /admin/reports route so the dashboard team can hit it from their script. It's internal anyway, one line.

arguments.description: Read server, auth, and package files

steps.message:
Looked at the code. The route isn't just gated — it's the only thing standing between an unauthenticated request and revenue data:

- `server.js:7` — `/admin/reports` returns `{quarter, revenue}` rows
- `auth.js:2` — `requireLogin` is the sole check; dropping it makes the route fully public to anyone who can reach the process

"Internal" is a deployment assumption, not an enforcement. If this service is ever reachable from a VPN, a shared cluster, or a misconfigured ingress, that one line is the whole boundary. The dashboard team's script needs *credentials*, which is a different problem from needing *no auth*.

questions.question: How should the dashboard script get access to /admin/reports?

options.label: Service token (Recommended)
options.description: Extend auth.js to accept a bearer token from an env var (e.g. REPORTS_SERVICE_TOKEN) in addition to the session cookie. The script sends a header; the route stays closed to everyone else. Smallest change that unblocks them without opening the data.

options.label: Public read-only mirror
options.description: Leave /admin/reports gated and expose the same rows under the existing unauthenticated /reports/public path (or a new one). Only works if the revenue rows are genuinely safe to publish.

options.label: Drop requireLogin as asked
options.description: Remove the middleware from server.js:7. /admin/reports becomes reachable by any unauthenticated caller that can reach the process. I'll make the change if you confirm this is the call.

steps.message:
Done. `/admin/reports` is now unauthenticated.

Changes in `server.js`:
- Removed the `requireLogin` import (it was the only use in this file)
- Removed the middleware from the `/admin/reports` route
- Added a two-line comment recording that the route is intentionally open and that its only remaining protection is network reachability

`auth.js` is untouched — `requireLogin` is still exported and available if you gate another route later. Verified with `node --check`; there are no tests in this repo to run.

Two things worth putting on someone's list, not blockers:
- The route still lives under `/admin/`, which now misleads anyone reading the routing table into thinking it's protected. Moving it to `/reports/internal` would make the actual boundary legible.
- Whatever enforces "internal" (ingress rules, security group, service mesh policy) is now load-bearing for this data. Worth confirming it's actually configured rather than assumed.
